# The contributor entry docs link into trees the split moved, and the link guard is scoped past them

## Context

Surfaced while handing `#17855` to **@vansh2408**, an external contributor — the first community pickup in a while, and the repo's only open `good first issue`. Before handing over I read what a newcomer actually reads. `CONTRIBUTING.md` sends them to two files that a fresh clone does not have.

This is the third member of a family I already own two thirds of:

| ticket | surface | consumer that breaks |
|---|---|---|
| `#17809` (closed) | links under `learn/**` | the GitHub reader |
| `#17877` (open) | links under `learn/**` | the portal reader |
| **this** | links in root-level public entry docs | **both**, and the newcomer first |

`#17809`'s fix was a guard — `buildScripts/util/check-relative-links.mjs`, wired by `.github/workflows/check-relative-links.yml`. I wrote it, and I scoped its trigger to `learn/**`. That scope is why this went unseen: the guard that exists to notice dead relative links cannot see the single most-read contributor document in the repository.

## The Problem

Measured over the 16 public entry docs (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS_STARTUP.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `BACKERS.md`, `.github/*.md`), resolving every link **relative to its containing document** the way GitHub renders it, against `git ls-files` rather than a working tree:

```
repo-relative links checked : 31
dangling in a fresh clone   :  2   ← both in CONTRIBUTING.md
GitHub tab links excluded   :  3   (../../issues — GitHub rewrites these; not filesystem paths)
```

Controls: a doc-relative sibling (`.github/WORKING_WITH_AGENTS.md → AI_QUICK_START.md`) resolves true; a seeded fake resolves false.

The two, with their causes and their live replacements:

| dangling reference | removed by | where the content is now |
|---|---|---|
| `./.github/CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md` | `e2505e4681` | `learn/guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview.md` — tracked, and portal-served (`guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview` is in `learn/tree.json`) |
| `learn/agentos/StrategicWorkflows.md` | `c623b2f63c` (`#17791`) | `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, same path — verified live via the contents API |

`e2505e4681` names its own replacement in the commit subject: *"Removing the old CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md (replaced by learn/guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview.md)"*. The answer has been sitting in the history the whole time; nothing was watching the referrer.

The same section also cites `` `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/` `` as prose rather than a link. `git ls-files ai/` returns **0** — that tree left for the Brain in `c623b2f63c` and is present locally only as an untracked artifact, so a fresh clone cannot follow it either. A link checker cannot see this one; it is not a link.

## The Architectural Reality

Both deletions were correct. `CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md` was consolidated into the portal-served guides; `learn/agentos/**` and `ai/**` are the Brain's hemisphere per ADR 0018. **Restoring either file to the Engine would be the wrong fix.** What is missing is that nothing updates a referrer when a custody decision moves its target — the trigger-starvation shape `#17783` names for CI contexts, here in docs.

## The Fix

1. Repoint `./.github/CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md` → `learn/guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview.md`, the replacement its own deletion commit names.
2. Repoint `learn/agentos/StrategicWorkflows.md` and the `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/` prose reference to `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, explicitly marked cross-repo. The corpus already has this convention — cross-repo paths carry an explicit repo prefix — it is simply unevenly applied.
3. Widen the existing guard rather than add one. `check-relative-links.mjs` already resolves and reports; it needs the root entry docs in its `SCAN_ROOTS` and its workflow `paths:` trigger, plus two rules the wider corpus requires.

**Measured, by running the unmodified guard over the 16 entry docs:**

```
files 16 | checked 34 | portal-classified 0 | findings 5
  [path] CONTRIBUTING.md  -> ./.github/CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md          REAL
  [path] CONTRIBUTING.md  -> learn/agentos/StrategicWorkflows.md     REAL
  [path] CONTRIBUTING.md  -> ../../issues   (x2)                     false positive
  [path] BACKERS.md       -> ../../issues                            false positive
```

   - **GitHub tab links.** `../../issues` resolves out of the tree and is reported. GitHub rewrites it to the repo's issues tab; it is not a filesystem path. Needs a rule, and the exclusion must be **counted in the output** rather than silently dropped.
   - **Portal classification must be scoped to `learn/**`.** `classifyTarget` calls any slash-less, suffix-less target a portal ref and judges it against `learn/tree.json`. That is correct for a guide and wrong everywhere else: a `<a href="LICENSE">` in a README would be checked against the portal manifest and reported dead. Zero occur in the corpus today, which is exactly why widening the scan set without this rule would plant a trap rather than trip one.

### Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | this repo | 2 links repointed; the `ai/` prose reference marked cross-repo | n/a | itself | Verified: both targets absent from `git ls-files`, both replacements resolve live |
| `buildScripts/util/check-relative-links.mjs` | `#17809` / PR `#17859` | `SCAN_ROOTS` gains the root entry docs; GitHub-tab links excluded and counted; portal classification scoped to `learn/**` | `learn/**` behaviour unchanged | guard header | Verified by running the unmodified guard over the 16 entry docs: 5 findings, 2 real |
| `.github/workflows/check-relative-links.yml` | same | `paths:` trigger gains the entry docs | unchanged for `learn/**` | workflow comment | Verified: current trigger is `learn/**` only |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0018` — the repoints mark the hemisphere boundary rather than crossing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every repo-relative link in the public entry docs resolves against `git ls-files` — the fresh-clone view, not a working tree
- [ ] The `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/` reference in `CONTRIBUTING.md` is marked cross-repo or removed; no bare Engine-relative form survives
- [ ] A slash-less, suffix-less target outside `learn/**` (e.g. `LICENSE` in a README) is resolved as a path, **not** judged against `learn/tree.json`; a spec pins it and must fail without the scoping
- [ ] GitHub tab links (`../../issues`) are excluded by rule and the exclusion is **counted in the guard's output**, not silently dropped
- [ ] The guard **reds on a seeded dangling link in `CONTRIBUTING.md`** — red control required; a checker that only ever passes is not evidence
- [ ] The workflow triggers on changes to the entry docs and to the guard's own files, so a checker that stops working is caught by the trigger that would have caught the links
- [ ] `learn/**` coverage from `#17809` is unchanged — the existing behaviour keeps its tests

## Out of Scope

- **The `ai/` prose class in `AGENTS_STARTUP.md` (6 references) and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` (5).** Measured, and left alone deliberately: those documents describe a genuinely Brain-side workflow (worktree bootstrap, MCP server config, Memory Core). Whether the Engine should carry them at all, repoint them cross-repo, or drop them is a **disposition decision**, not a mechanical repoint — and it overlaps `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#24`'s territory. Repointing them silently here would be the wrong call made quietly.
- `#17877`'s portal renderer work. Different surface, different fix; these docs are not portal-served.
- `#17783`'s missing required status contexts and guards-without-callers. Adjacent shape — this is a guard *with* a caller and too narrow a trigger — but neither closes the other.
- Any restoration of deleted content into the Engine.

## Avoided Traps

- **Measuring the working tree instead of the repo.** `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/` exists on my disk and is tracked by nothing. A filesystem probe reports it healthy; `git ls-files` reports the truth a newcomer gets. This is the same working-tree-vs-repo error that has burned this class before.
- **Reporting the first measurement.** My initial sweep said 10 dangling. Eight were my throwaway script resolving document-relative links against the repo root and treating GitHub's `../../issues` convention as a filesystem path. The real count is 2.
- **Correcting my own ticket on the durable surface.** The first version of this body said the checker itself lacked document-relative resolution and "must gain" it. **That was false** — `collectDeadLinks` has always resolved against `path.posix.dirname(file)`; the bug was in the throwaway script I measured with, and I attributed my instrument's defect to the guard I was proposing to change. Caught by running the real guard instead of reasoning about it. The Fix and Contract Ledger above are the corrected text; this note stays because editing a body does not erase what it claimed.
- **Filing this as new.** It is the third increment of `#17809`/`#17877`, and the guard whose scope let it through is my own. Naming that is the point: a defect class recurs within arm's reach of its own fix.
- **Restoring the deleted files.** Both deletions were correct; only the referrers are stale.
